extracted.intended_audience: readers of art history, students and practitioners of painting and mosaic (Renaissance art specialists and general art-historical readers)
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria for judging the skill, technique, and professional conduct of Renaissance painters and craftsmen, drawn from Vasari's biographical narratives and examples. Focuses on artistic excellence, technical knowledge, materials, consistency of practice, and effects of commerce/avarice on an artist's career.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value of excellence in a noble art
rubrics_metrics.description: How honourable and profitable it is to be excellent in a noble art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vasari argues that excellence brings honour, profit, and social elevation (example: Taddeo Gaddi's industry and labours left his family means and fame; successors were adorned with ecclesiastical dignities).

rubrics_metrics.name: Industry and sustained labour (diligence)
rubrics_metrics.description: An artist's industry and labours are central to acquiring fame and means.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Persistent work and study lead to advancement; contrast with those who fall back through negligence with age. Exemplified by Taddeo's industriousness vs Agnolo's later negligence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of avarice/commerce impeding artistic study
rubrics_metrics.description: Avarice or a turn to commerce often prevents the intellect from rising to excellence in art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vasari notes Agnolo, 'given more to traffic and to trading than to the art of painting', produced uneven work; anti-pattern: prioritizing trade over study reduces artistic development and output.

rubrics_metrics.name: Realism and careful depiction of physical detail
rubrics_metrics.description: Accurate, convincing depiction of physical states and effects (e.g., the corruption of a dead body) enhances the work's impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Agnolo's Resurrection of Lazarus – discoloured grave-clothes, livid/yellowish marks round the eyes, and figures reacting in varied, believable ways; such realism was judged 'so excellent' by contemporaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Variety and accurate rendering of costumes, tasks, and attitudes
rubrics_metrics.description: Scenes that present diverse costumes, head-dresses, and a range of activities executed with correctness and variety are praiseworthy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: the scene round Our Lady with many maidens spinning, sewing, winding thread, weaving, etc., 'all passing well conceived and executed by Agnolo' — variety and correct depiction of daily tasks are indicators of skill.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design (drawing/composition) versus colouring (colour technique)
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish between the quality of design (compositional invention/drawing) and the quality of colouring; both matter but are distinct strengths/weaknesses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: S. Croce principal chapel 'executed with much mastery of handling but not with much design, for only the colouring is beautiful'. Guidance: beautiful colouring alone does not substitute for strong design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency of zeal and absence of caprice
rubrics_metrics.description: Consistent zeal (steady effort) rather than working 'by caprice' produces more uniformly excellent works.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vasari criticises Agnolo for working 'now with more zeal and now with less', yielding uneven outcomes (some frescoes very good, others poor).

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical mastery of media (fresco, distemper, mosaic, panel work)
rubrics_metrics.description: Competence in the technical processes of the medium (fresco, distemper, mosaic, panel painting) is a core standard of craftsmanship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples and methods: Agnolo painted in distemper panels and frescoes; he restored mosaics by cutting slabs to half thickness and joining with cement of mastic and wax; Cennino's treatise describes fresco, distemper, size, gum, and gold-application techniques. Technical execution affects aesthetic result and durability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Durability and proper materials/assembly for restoration
rubrics_metrics.description: Selection of proper materials and methods that ensure long-term durability (resistance to rain, fire, decay) is an evaluative standard in restoration and architectural works.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Agnolo's mosaic restoration—laying new marbles, pieces overlapped at joinings, slabs cut to half thickness and cemented with mastic and wax—resulted in protection from rain damage; he also advised vaulting and rebuilding cornices to prevent fire damage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical counsel and planning in architectural/civic works
rubrics_metrics.description: Ability to propose and implement practical architectural solutions and civic improvements (e.g., vaulting, battlements, cornice rebuilding) is part of a master's contribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vasari credits Agnolo with counsel that led to rebuilding the upper cornice, making the vaulting of the Great Hall of the Palace, and adding battlements to the Palace—guidance emphasizes usefulness/protection as well as adornment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excellence in small-scale narrative/detail work (predella and miniatures)
rubrics_metrics.description: Skill in composing and executing small figures and narrative episodes (predella panels, small stories) is a distinct measure of talent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Agnolo's panel for S. Pancrazio – 'the best of this work... the predella alone, which is all full of little figures, divided into eight stories' — fine detail work praised.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expressive rendering of faces and physiognomy
rubrics_metrics.description: The ability to give 'very beautiful expressions' to faces (children, women, old men) is a valued artistic quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Stefano da Verona was 'excellent in giving very beautiful expressions to the faces' which made his works widely imitated; facial expression is singled out as an indicator of mastery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Knowledge of pigments, colour-ground preparation, and mordants
rubrics_metrics.description: Understanding the nature of colours (minerals and earth-colours), distempers, sizes, gesso application, grinding colours, and mordants for gold is an essential craft standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cennino's book (a pupil of Agnolo) treats these technical matters; Vasari lists pigments then lacking (dark red earths, cinabrese, vitreous greens) and later discoveries (umber, giallo santo, smalts) — guidance: technical material knowledge improves practice and preserves works.

rubrics_metrics.name: Draughtsmanship / drawing skill
rubrics_metrics.description: Ability in drawing and draughtsmanship (preparatory drawings) is a component of artistic excellence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vasari notes Agnolo 'was not excellent in draughtsmanship, in so far as is shown by some drawings by his hand' — drawings can reveal limits in an artist's skill.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transmission of methods through teaching and writing
rubrics_metrics.description: A master's value is also measured by the instruction and codification of methods (pupils, treatises) that pass techniques to successors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Cennino di Drea wrote a manual of working methods learned from Agnolo covering fresco, distemper, gesso, gold application; disciples (e.g., Stefano da Verona, Michele da Milano) carried the master's influence into other regions.
